seed: uk electronic music evolution, acid house, second summer of love, breakbeat hardcore

required_records.title: Oochy Koochy
required_records.why: source 5 credits acid house pioneers in the London context; Baby Ford appears in early electronic synthpop-to-acid histories as a parallel development

required_records.title: LFO
required_records.why: source 5 documents breakbeat hardcore emergence in UK rave scene; LFO's warehouse mix is canonical for early 1990s hard house/breakbeat

required_records.title: DJs Take Control
required_records.why: foundational breakbeat hardcore track from SL2, part of the 1990-1993 consolidation of UK rave sound

required_records.title: Original Nuttah
required_records.why: source 5 and catalogue: jungle's breakthrough moment on the amen break; one of the genre's most sampled records

required_records.title: Inner City Life
required_records.why: source 5 credits Goldie as the mainline between hard breakbeat and liquid drum and bass; this track is the definition of the crossover

required_records.title: Unfinished Sympathy
required_records.why: source 5 places Massive Attack in post-rave electronica; Unfinished Sympathy is the group's most influential track spanning UK dance and art-world contexts

required_records.title: Chemical Beats
required_records.why: parallel to Massive Attack; The Chemical Brothers carry big beat out of rave context into the crossover moment of the late 1990s

required_records.title: Xtal
required_records.why: source 5 and source 6: Aphex Twin appears in ambient and intelligent dance music histories as the IDM founder; Xtal is from Selected Ambient Works 85-92

required_records.title: Anti War Dub
required_records.why: source 5: founders of 2000s UK bass movement; Mala's production work on Anti War Dub defines the dubstep half-step bass philosophy

required_records.title: Firestarter
required_records.why: source 5 credits The Prodigy repeatedly as the bridge from breakbeat hardcore to 1990s crossover. The group was named three times on the page with no record of theirs to hear. Not Charly, which the breakbeat guide carries: media is not reused across guides.

required_records.title: Journey Down The Thames
required_records.why: source 5 documents both as the DJs who consolidated breakbeat hardcore on radio and in clubs. Both were named on the page with nothing to hear. DJs, so the evidence is a set, and this one is on Hospital Records' own channel and in our catalogue.

known_gaps.title: Acid Tracks — Phuture, 1987: named, not embedded
known_gaps.why: Now named in the prose with DJ Pierre and Trax Records, which closes the absence. No embed: every YouTube upload found is a fan vinyl rip and there is no upload on the label's or artist's own channel, so under WRITING.md none of them qualifies. Spotify has the track (7BKjoKthIrz3m2XxIrLCtG) but this guide's media is YouTube video cards throughout, and mixing one Spotify player into that grid is a design decision, not a repair.

known_gaps.title: Correction: Rinse FM was never missing from this page
known_gaps.why: The recorded gap said the page had no reference to the station. It has two, one of them a linked Guardian piece on twenty years of Rinse. The note was wrong and is kept as a correction rather than deleted.
